title: Decompose SLO signals to suppress transient spikes and improve alert fidelity
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Follow-up from the Feb capacity regression postmortem: alerts were dominated by short-lived spike traffic that inflated burn-rate signals and caused unnecessary paging. This ticket breaks down SLO signals into transient vs sustained components, implements hysteresis for burn-rate alerts, and adds a lightweight signal-quality dashboard so ops can tune thresholds without repeated pager storms.
acceptance_criteria: Alerting system emits separate 'sustained-burn' and 'transient-spike' metrics for each SLO window
Paging only occurs for sustained-burn incidents after configurable hysteresis is crossed
Signal-quality dashboard shows false-positive rate, median burst-duration, and percent of alerts suppressed per service
Runbook updated with new escalation flow and suppression playbook and validated in canary for two services
No increase in true-positive time-to-detect for regressions in a 2-week canary (<= 5% delta)
proposed_actions: Implement two-path signal decomposition in the alerting pipeline: short-window spike detector (1m/5m) and long-window burn estimator (5m/1h)
Add exponential decay weighting to burn-rate calculation so very short spikes contribute <10% to burn over 1h window
Introduce hysteresis and cool-down: require burn > threshold for two consecutive long windows before paging
Create metric 'alert_signal_quality' that tracks suppressed_alerts / total_alerts and integrates with console
Add synthetic-traffic flagging: exclude or downweight alerts correlated with canary/chaos tests via request metadata
Ship a lightweight dashboard (Console) and a PagerDuty integration toggle for 'non-paging only' alerts

2026-03-03: Ran offline backtest over Jan-Feb production traces: decay-weighting reduced candidate pager events by 42% while keeping true regression detection recall at 96%
2026-03-04: UX mockups for console dashboard uploaded to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b-alert-fidelity-mocks; PM feedback: add per-route attribution

Blockers: need filtering keys for synthetic traffic; awaiting product decision on propagation of 'traffic_origin' header (PRD link below)
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Chose decay-weighted burn calculation over rigid sliding-window majority because it reduces latency penalty for sustained regressions while dampening single-point spikes
Hysteresis duration set initially to two long windows (default 10m) to balance pager reduction vs detection time; can be tuned by service tier
Will not apply aggressive suppression for P0 services by default; policy will be service-configurable to avoid masking high-impact regressions
Aggregation granularity: use 1m buckets for spike detector to align with existing ingestion; moving to sub-minute increases compute cost and complexity
